p1_findings.finding: The runner accepts public environment variables proving only that the canonical wrapper file with the expected SHA exists. It neither proves wrapper execution nor repeats the wrapper's literal host/GPU gate. The attempt and verifier bind the wrapper file hash, not launch ancestry or host/GPU receipt values.
p1_findings.impact: Direct execution of the unmodified exact runner can bypass the claimed unique wrapper and its host/GPU checks while producing an exact-seven attempt that the current payload verifier can accept.
p1_findings.required_fix: Move the literal hostname/GPU name/UUID/driver/memory-total gate into the exact runner before attempt creation, seal the observed values in the initial receipt, and make the payload verifier require the exact fields and values. Fresh-review all changed identities. Do not add only another caller-controlled marker.

p2_findings.finding: Critical package versions are checked pre/post, but site-package files or wheel RECORD contents are not sealed.
p2_findings.impact: Same-version local package-code drift is outside the immutable runtime identity.
p2_findings.recommendation: Seal critical wheel RECORD/install-tree identities or explicitly retain this as a payload-only provenance limitation.

p2_findings.finding: Preflight rejects -e and -L for canonical targets, but the post-start EXIT trap tests the canonical output with -e only.
p2_findings.impact: A post-start dangling symlink cannot pass the verifier but may survive rollback and cause one-shot denial or operator confusion.

authorization.next_action: Repair M633-P1-01 in runner receipt and verifier, reseal the launch chain, and request a fresh static hammer.
